domain_model: Each side uses paired boundary correspondence and normalized centerline-to-boundary width u=0..1. No degree subdivisions, half-degree rings, or fake shells.
geometry_source: Phase 2.36f HTML DATA payload; centerline/leftBoundary/rightBoundary/polygon copied unchanged
goal: Merge contour-density intelligence into one coherent topographic pressure surface without regressing to blur fog or overcorrecting into diagrammatic contour art.

1_carrier_line_continuous_and_saturated_.notes: Carrier is drawn last from the same station geometry in all modes and appears continuous in both MC and ASC screenshots.

2_white_or_washed_out_centerline_artifac.notes: No white carrier stroke is used and no white centerline artifact is visible in the first-run screenshots.

3_structural_bands_merged_or_still_strip.notes: Unified pressure and premium hybrid reduce visible striation, but ridge compression and some micro-laminations can still read as structural marks/stripes if pushed further.

4_topographic_pressure_not_blur_glow.notes: The SVG vector surface reduces alpha-fog behavior and reads more structurally than Phases 2.37/2.38, but the unified surface still uses translucent ribbons and may be judged too soft by visual QA.

5_pressure_consistent_without_random_poc.notes: Pressure is more consistent than Phase 2.39 because the hard contours were softened, but MC still has subtle local density variation where micro-laminations and ribbons overlap.

6_field_inside_locked_phase_236f_mask.notes: The renderer uses paired correspondence between the locked centerline, leftBoundary, and rightBoundary polylines; no sampled field extends beyond those side domains.

7_mc_and_asc_both_improved.notes: Both MC and ASC improve over Phase 2.39 in carrier continuity and reduced line-art dominance; ASC especially benefits from reduced hard contour visibility.

strict_visual_methodology_audit.smallest_next_correction: Choose one candidate, likely unified_pressure or premium_hybrid, then tune density/contrast in a single-mode artifact: reduce ridge_compression-style marks, slightly strengthen carrier/near-ridge pressure, and keep outer ribbons subtle without adding blur.

rendering_method: SVG vector surface: translucent normalized-domain ribbons for continuity plus low-contrast compressed micro-laminations; carrier drawn last as saturated blue ridge. No raster ImageData field, blur filter, gaussian feather, or white carrier stroke.

visual_assessment.field_reads_as_structure_rather_than_blu: mostly; unified_pressure and premium_hybrid best balance structure with surface continuity
visual_assessment.needs_next_pass: Human visual QA should decide between unified_pressure and premium_hybrid, then tune density/contrast in a single candidate.
visual_assessment.overcorrects_into_diagram_art: pressure_terraces removed; ridge_compression remains most at risk if density is pushed further
risks: Unified surface still uses translucent ribbons and could be perceived as soft wash if density is too low.
Micro-laminations must remain faint enough to merge rather than become stripes.
Further tuning should reduce mode count and converge on one restrained candidate.
visual_assessment.visible_striation_reduced: partially; individual contour lines are less dominant than Phase 2.39, but ridge-compression mode can still show visible structural marks
